summary: Verified fix for Google 403 by switching to Emergent-managed OAuth. Backend pytest 4/4 PASS on new /api/auth/google/session (missing header 400, invalid session 401, never 500) + legacy safe. UI Playwright 4/4 PASS: Google button navigates to https://auth.emergentagent.com/?redirect=<origin>/ (no accounts.google.com), fake session_id callback redirects to /login without blank crash, email OTP path intact, authenticated ChatApp still renders with sidebar+composer via QA token.
critical_code_review_comments: test_credentials.md still says 'Google login: DIRECT Google OAuth 2.0 (accounts.google.com)' — outdated after the switch to Emergent-managed OAuth. Recommend updating docs to note login now goes to auth.emergentagent.com.
Legacy /api/auth/google endpoint and GoogleCallback.jsx / /auth/google route still exist (harmless). Consider removing to reduce attack surface and confusion.
AuthCallback.jsx swallows all errors with an empty catch — fine for redirect UX, but a toast('Google login failed') would be a nicer signal for the user before navigating to /login.

AuthContext.checkAuth() runs even when a Bearer token exists in localStorage but no session_id hash — that's correct; just noting that when /auth/me returns 401 the app immediately shows /login, which is expected.
test_credentials: QA token: localStorage.setItem('claus_token','test_session_qa_01') → user_testqa01 / qa@claus.test. Verified working.
seed_data_creation: None. Existing QA user & session already seeded from prior iterations.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Google login now goes through Emergent-managed OAuth (https://auth.emergentagent.com/?redirect=<origin>/). Backend endpoint is POST /api/auth/google/session with header X-Session-ID; returns 400 without header, 401 for invalid session (calls demobackend.emergentagent.com/auth/v1/env/oauth/session-data). Playwright cannot complete a real Google login (no real Google account), so verification is limited to (a) intercepting the click's navigation target and (b) verifying the callback flow gracefully handles an invalid session_id. Legacy /api/auth/google direct-OAuth endpoint still present but unused.

rca of the issue: Root cause of original Google 403 (from iteration 1): direct OAuth 2.0 client in a non-verified Google Cloud project only permits test users listed in the consent screen; other Google accounts (including QA agents) receive 'Non disponi dell'autorizzazione'. Fix applied by main agent: replaced direct OAuth with Emergent-managed OAuth (auth.emergentagent.com → demobackend.emergentagent.com/auth/v1/env/oauth/session-data). This uses a pre-verified OAuth app so any Google user can sign in without any Google Cloud config. Verified: (1) button now targets auth.emergentagent.com, (2) backend /api/auth/google/session accepts X-Session-ID and calls Emergent session-data endpoint, (3) fake session id → 401 → clean redirect to /login.
